SMARTA VARIANT NOT MODELLED -- attempted 2026-08-11, reverted after finding it would ship wrong, not just incomplete. The natural fix (a second sampradaya='smarta' row, per the krishna-janmashtami precedent) does NOT work with the current engine: calculateObservancesForYearCorrected's occurrencesMap is keyed by SLUG ONLY, and its final per-rule loop does not re-check isPublishableForYear for each row sharing that slug -- it just fans the one shared map value out to every row. A deferred second row therefore does NOT get suppressed; it silently computes the SAME date as the included row (verified directly: both resolved to 2026-07-11), which would have published 07-11 labelled as BOTH 'Smarta' and 'Vaishnava', when the source says Smarta is 07-10 -- worse than the single-row state, because it would assert something false rather than merely omit something true. krishna-janmashtami's existing two rows have the identical latent gap; it has never surfaced there because both of its rows are identical in every gating-relevant field (masa, tithi, system, launch_status), so which one 'wins' the shared map slot never mattered. Currently inert: both USE_CORRECTED_MASA and USE_CONDITION_EVALUATOR are false, so nothing exercises this path in production today. Real follow-up, correctly scoped as engine work, not a rules.json edit: give same-slug variant rows independently gate-able identity (e.g. keyed on slug+sampradaya, not bare slug) before any future variant pair with DIFFERING launch_status/derivability can ship. Filed rather than patched under time pressure -- the Smarta date (2026-07-10) is preserved in the citation above for when this is fixed.
